description:
A multi-platform GUI SSH terminal with a files panel, a built-in editor and split panes.

rulogman is a desktop SSH client written in Rust and drawn with gpui, the
GPU-accelerated UI framework behind the Zed editor. Connections are saved as
profiles — host, user, password or private key — and open in tabs that can be split
into panes, each with its own connection and its own scrollback. The terminal itself
is alacritty_terminal, so colors, cursor addressing, the alternate screen and
full-screen programs such as vim, tmux and htop behave as they do in any other
terminal.

Beside the terminal sits a files panel that browses the session's filesystem over
SFTP on a channel of the same connection, with drag-and-drop transfers and a
breadcrumb path. Right-clicking a file opens it in a built-in editor tab with line
numbers, find and replace, undo and syntax highlighting for seventeen formats, and
Ctrl+S writes it back over the connection it came from. Port forwarding rules,
including a SOCKS proxy, are saved with the profile and open as soon as the shell is
up, and profiles can be imported from the OpenSSH client's config file.

Not every terminal is remote: local shells are first-class too, with PowerShell, cmd
and every installed WSL distribution offered from the start screen. Host keys are
checked on the trust-on-first-use convention, and passwords and key passphrases go
to the Windows Credential Manager rather than to any configuration file. Themes and
terminal color schemes are picked independently, scheme files use Windows
Terminal's format, and the interface is available in eight languages.
rulogman 0.6.7 — ARM64 Windows and Linux, Intel Mac and AppImage downloads, a Linux build that no longer needs libxkbcommon-x11, and rugpui 0.1.18.
- Three more downloads, and an AppImage. Each release now also carries builds for Windows on ARM64 (aarch64-pc-windows-msvc), Intel Macs (x86_64-apple-darwin) and ARM64 Linux (aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu), each built on a machine of its own architecture, and Linux also ships as an AppImage that runs where it is. The winget package lists the ARM64 installer, and the Homebrew cask is updated with each release and carries both macOS builds.
- The Linux build no longer needs libxkbcommon-x11. xkbcommon, keyboard handling included, is built into the binary together with libxcb-xkb, so the program no longer exits at once on a desktop that does not install libxkbcommon-x11; from the system it asks only for glibc, libgcc_s and libxcb. install.sh no longer checks for xkbcommon.
- The updater installs these builds in place. A copy on one of the new targets downloads its own build, and an AppImage replaces its own image file, instead of opening the release page.
- The about dialog opens the project page at https://xcomart.github.io/rulogman/ instead of the repository.
- Shared libraries are updated to rugpui 0.1.18, and async-executor moves past its yanked release. UI dependencies and framework patches are pinned to rugpui's published release commit.

Requirements
- Linux: glibc 2.35 or newer: Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12 and later, or a distribution built on them, MX Linux 23 among them.
- Linux AppImage: the same glibc, and FUSE to mount the image (the fuse3 package, which desktop installs of those distributions include). Without FUSE, start it with --appimage-extract-and-run.
